% Pattern: head/case. A case or a step head that gives its number as a word
% ("First case"), glued to the title ("STEP-1", "Step1", "Step $1$"), with a
% parenthesis ("Case 1)", "Case (a)") or with no number ("Case: ...", "Final
% step") is an item. Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1 status=here
% want proof-1 proof - proves=theorem-1
% want head-1 other/case 1
% want head-2 other/case 2
% want head-3 other/case 1
% want head-4 other/case 2
% want head-5 other/case 3
% want head-6 other/case 1
% want head-7 other/case (a)
% want head-8 other/case -
% want head-9 other/case -
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
\begin{theorem}
Every compact space is bounded.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Take a cover by balls.

\textbf{First case:} the cover is finite.

\textbf{Second case:} the cover is infinite.

\noindent\textbf{STEP-1} Take a finite subcover.

\indent \textbf{Step2.} Take the largest radius.

{\em Step $3$}. Add the distances.

\emph{Case 1).} The radius is one.

\paragraph{Case (a): the set is an interval.} Measure it.

\textit{Case: the set is a point.} It is plain.

{\bf Final step.} Sum up.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
